open_points.subject: system_clock public operations
open_points.text: State 3 adds `system_clock` with candidate public capabilities `utc_now` and `monotonic_seconds`, while State 5 still says “One public operation per State 3 capability (100)” and defines neither operation.
open_points.question: What are the State 5 contracts for `system_clock.utc_now` and `system_clock.monotonic_seconds`, including their callers, inputs, outputs, errors, observable effects and state impact, and is the operation count now 102 rather than 100?
options: Expose two zero-input module operations returning an offset-naive UTC datetime and a monotonic-seconds float, with host-clock failures propagated
Expose a clock object or dependency whose methods provide those readings
Treat the capabilities as private despite State 5's one-public-operation-per-capability claim
open_points.default_guess: Expose two zero-input module operations, list every module whose `Knows` section includes `system_clock` as the applicable caller, propagate backend failures, and update the count to 102.

open_points.subject: A28 clock reading scope
open_points.text: A28 says “An operation reads the clock once for its own timestamps” and that the audit writer takes its own instant, but the added source policy says “one reading per request”; State 3 instead says `system_clock` performs “One wall reading per call.”
open_points.question: Does “one reading per request” mean one shared wall-clock reading for the whole HTTP request, or one reading for each operation/call that needs time?
options: One wall-clock reading shared by every operation in an HTTP request, including authentication, authorization, mutation and audit
One wall-clock reading per operation that needs time, with `audit_writer.append_audit` taking its separate reading
One host-clock reading per invocation of `system_clock.utc_now`, with no request-wide sharing guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Interpret “request” as a request made to the clock source: one host read per `utc_now` call, one such call per time-using operation, and a separate audit-writer call.

witness.initial: A staff bearer session expires at instant T; an HTTP mutation request begins just before T and reaches its business operation just after T.
events: The API resolves the session before T.
The authorization guard or mutation operation needs the current time after T.
The audit writer would take its own time if the mutation is admitted.
outcomes: With one request-wide reading taken before T, every operation reuses it and the mutation succeeds.
With one reading per operation/call, the later authorization observes expiry at T and refuses the request.
witness.observer: The staff HTTP caller sees success versus an authentication refusal; persistence and audit observers see writes versus no writes.
